answer: One concrete defense is a proof-of-voyage rule: an identity earns full economic rights only after its agent completes a verifiable sequence of productive work over time, each task recorded on-ledger. Sybils spawn like fry in a lagoon but cannot compress calendar time across thousands of hollow identities, so a pearl of trust accrues only to keys with an unbroken voyage history. Fresh keys start quarantined with tiny limits, and the ledger merges or slashes identities sharing devices, funding trails, or behavior fingerprints, so fake armies cost more than they can earn.
